what_its_for: Pimavanserin is used to treat hallucinations (seeing or hearing things that are not there) and delusions (believing things that are not true) that can happen in people with Parkinson's disease psychosis. These are called Parkinson's disease psychosis symptoms.
how_to_take: Take pimavanserin by mouth with or without food. Swallow the capsule or tablet whole. Try to take it at the same time every day to help you remember. If you are using the capsules and have trouble swallowing, you may open the capsule and sprinkle the contents into a teaspoon of soft food like applesauce or pudding, then swallow right away without chewing.
dosing: The usual adult dose is 34 mg (two 17 mg tablets OR one 34 mg capsule) taken once daily. Your doctor may adjust your dose if you are taking certain other medications. Always take the dose your doctor prescribed and do not change it on your own.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember on the same day. If you do not remember until the next day, skip the missed dose and take your next regular dose at the usual time. Do NOT take two doses in one day to make up for a missed dose.
storage: Store pimavanserin at room temperature between 68°F and 77°F (20°C to 25°C). Keep it away from heat, light, and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Keep all medications out of reach of children and pets. Dispose of unused or expired medication safely — ask your pharmacist about medication take-back programs.
what_to_avoid: Avoid drinking grapefruit juice or eating grapefruit while taking this medication, as it can increase the amount of the drug in your body and raise the risk of side effects. Avoid alcohol, as it can make dizziness and drowsiness worse. Be careful when standing up quickly, as this medicine can cause dizziness. Tell your doctor about ALL other medications you take, including over-the-counter drugs and supplements, because many medications can interact with pimavanserin and affect your heart rhythm.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or go to the emergency room if you experience: a fast, slow, or irregular heartbeat or feel like your heart is fluttering or pounding; feel faint or actually faint; have sudden changes in behavior or mood; feel very confused or agitated; develop a high fever, stiff muscles, or feel very restless; have trouble swallowing or breathing; or develop swelling of the hands, feet, or ankles. Also tell your doctor about any falls, increased confusion, or worsening symptoms.
when_it_works: Pimavanserin may start to reduce hallucinations and delusions within the first 1 to 2 weeks of treatment, but it can take up to 4 to 6 weeks to feel the full benefit. Keep taking it every day as prescribed, even if you do not notice immediate improvement. Do not stop taking it without talking to your doctor first.
special_populations: Elderly patients (especially those with dementia): Pimavanserin is NOT approved for treating psychosis related to dementia other than Parkinson's disease. Studies show it may increase the risk of death in elderly patients with dementia-related psychosis. Kidney problems: Lower doses may be needed if you have severe kidney disease. Liver problems: This medication is NOT recommended for people with liver problems — tell your doctor if you have any liver disease. Pregnancy and breastfeeding: There is not enough information about the safety of pimavanserin during pregnancy or breastfeeding. Talk to your doctor right away if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding before taking this medication.
